disclosures.text: A coupling head having a coupling head rotation axis.
The coupling head includes three drive surfaces.
The three drive surfaces of the coupling head are rotationally symmetrical through 120° with respect to the coupling head rotation axis.
A coupling member having a coupling member rotation axis.
The coupling member includes three first, right open helicoidal drive surfaces.
The axis of the first helicoidal drive surfaces substantially coincides with the coupling member rotation axis.
The three drive surfaces of the coupling member are rotationally symmetrical through 120° with respect to the coupling member rotation axis.
The coupling member further includes three second drive surfaces.
Each second drive surface is mirror symmetric to a respective first right open helicoidal drive surface.
The mirror symmetry is in a respective axial-radial plane of symmetry.
The coupling head and coupling member are detachably couplable.
In a coupled state, their respective rotational axes are aligned.
The coupling head is rotatable to drive each of its three drive surfaces.
Each drive surface of the coupling head is in contact with one of a respective first drive surface or second drive surface of the coupling member.
Driving the coupling head in contact with the coupling member results in exertion of both torque and an axially directed force on the coupling member.
The axially directed force is independent of whether the coupling member is driven clockwise or counter-clockwise.

A floor cleaning device, comprising an elongate, substantially cylindrical brush rotatably mounted, a motor mechanism to drive the brush at at least 2500 rpm, and a drive coupling assembly between the motor and brush, where the coupling hea
Each drive surface of the coupling head and coupling member has a radial extent of ≦15 mm.
The radial extent is the length of the largest radius of the respective drive surface.
The drive surfaces of the coupling head and coupling member have a radial extent of ≦9 mm.
The coupling member defines a coupling head reception cavity.
The cavity is bounded by a side wall that extends around the coupling member rotation axis.
The cavity provides for three radially inwardly protruding drive cams.
Each drive cam has a respective one of the first drive surfaces.
Each of the three radially inwardly protruding drive cams provides for a leading first drive surface and a trailing second drive surface, viewed tangentially.
The coupling head reception cavity is further bounded by a generally planar back wall.
The back wall extends perpendicular to the coupling member rotation axis.
The back wall connects to the side wall.
The coupling head includes a generally triangular drive section.
The triangular drive section provides for the coupling head's drive surfaces.
The drive surfaces are interconnected by connecting surfaces.
Each drive surface of the coupling head includes a slight convex curvature, seen in a plane perpendicular to the coupling head rotation axis.
Each drive surface of the coupling head has a convex curvature whose center lies substantially on the coupling head rotation axis.
The curvature is seen in a plane substantially transverse to a respective drive surface and containing the coupling head rotation axis.
The back wall of the coupling head reception cavity includes a central opening or recess.
The coupling head comprises a central nose that protrudes axially from the triangular drive section.
The opening or recess is configured to receive the nose in the coupled condition.
A brush assembly with an elongate, substantially cylindrical brush.
The brush extends between a first end and a second end.
The brush is configured to be rotatably mounted at said ends in a floor cleaning device.
One of the brush ends is provided with one of a coupling head or a coupling member of a drive coupling assembly.
A floor cleaning device comprising a motor mechanism.
The motor mechanism is configured to drive the brush into rotation at a rotational speed of at least 2500 rpm.
A drive coupling assembly is disposed between the motor mechanism and the brush.
During operation, torque from the motor mechanism is transferred to the brush via the drive coupling assembly.
A force directed along the longitudinal axis of the brush is transferred via the drive coupling assembly.
